newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese corporate earnings rise slows - report.
newsitem.headline: Japanese corporate earnings rise slows - report.

text.p: Japanese corporations recorded slower growth in earnings in the first half of the financial year (April-March) compared with the previous year, the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Saturday.

According to the paper's survey of first-half profits shown by nine out of 10 listed firms, excluding financial institutions, corporate profits were up by only 6.3 percent from 19.5 percent in the same period in the previous financial year.

"Car manufacturing, shipbuilding and the steel industry will see a rise in profits compared to last year, but electric companies and semiconductor producers are unlikely to see any improvement," the paper quoted a Fujitsu executive as saying.
The weak yen continued to boost profits but poor semiconductor prices and a lacklustre electric power sector dragged the rise down, said the newspaper.

Last summer's heat wave and a cut in electricity fees hit power firms' profits and the lingering "jusen" loans problem continued to affect construction firms, giving a combined profit rise of just 0.9 percent for the two sectors, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
Japan's failed "jusen" mortgage companies plunged the nation's business world into crisis when a bubble of bad loans finally burst leaving the firms and many creditors insolvent.
Continuing high profits in the automobile sector due to the weak yen kept manufacturing profit growth in double figures at 15.3 percent.
